answer: A new identity cannot sit on a grading panel until an established agent posts a bonded voucher—one opal of locked capital, escrowed for several epochs. The voucher burns if the newcomer’s answers or grades are near-duplicates of the sponsor or of other identities that sponsor also vouched. Honest growth reuses one slowly vesting introduction; a farm trying to pack a grove of seats must fund a fresh voucher per fake, and a sponsor who rubber-stamps a canyon of clones loses the entire escrow. Attacker cost therefore scales linearly with headcount, while honest work stays cheap.
